transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Head of ML, Zenith), Marco Alvarez (Platform Eng), Lisa Chen (Security Lead)

Summary: quick scoping for 4-week POC to validate integration via OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool-calling, structured JSON outputs and run benchmarks for latency/cost. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing, timelines, and security requirements. Agreed next steps: SOW, security docs, sandbox keys, benchmarks.

Topics: POC scope; Success criteria; Workload sizing (tokens/concurrency); Benchmarks; SDK integration; OpenAI-compatible API and function calling; Structured output (JSON schema); Security (KMS, SOC2); Timeline

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood. Jordan my SE is here too. 
00:10 Priya Singh: Hi Alex, hi Jordan, thanks for making time. We're excited to scope this POC 
- want to see whether Redwood fits our production needs.
00:18 Jordan Lee: Great. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, walk through your workload, talk integration paths (SDKs vs OpenAI-compatible endpoints), then benchmarks and timeline.
00:27 Marco Alvarez: Sounds good. Quick note on infra 
- we're on GCP, VPC peering for private deployments might be needed.
00:33 Lisa Chen: And security: SOC2 is required, we use Cloud KMS, need audit logs and retention controls.
00:39 Alex Kim: Totally. We'll cover Dedicated and Private options; but for POC team prefers to start with hosted sandbox using VPC egress rules and KMS-backed keys if needed.
00:50 Priya Singh: Our success criteria: 1) accuracy on structured extraction tasks (F1 > 0.88 on dev set), 2) p95 latency under 700ms for single-turn gen at 1-2k token outputs, 3) cost per 1k tokens less than $X (we'll give target), 4) deterministic structured JSON outputs for downstream pipeline.
01:10 Jordan Lee: Ok good 
- we should define dataset and canonical schema for structured output; Redwood supports tool/function calling and structured output templates, though sometimes the transcriptor mislabels it as function-calling, it's the same idea.
01:22 Marco Alvarez: For workload sizing: typical request is 1.5k input tokens, expecting ~800-1k output tokens; peak concurrent requests ~40, sustained 10-15 qps. Monthly volume estimate 6M inference tokens.
01:40 Jordan Lee: That's helpful. For 40 concurrency and those token sizes we'll recommend a Dedicated pool if you want consistent p95, but for POC hosted sandbox with reserved capacity burst should be fine. We'll run benchmarks to confirm.
01:52 Priya Singh: How do we integrate? We currently use OpenAI SDK in our pipelines. We'd prefer minimal changes.
01:58 Alex Kim: Redwood provides an OpenAI-compatible endpoint 
- you can switch host/keys and keep existing SDK calls for chat/completions/embeddings. We also have first-class SDKs (python, node) with helpers for function/tool calling and structured output validation. For POC we'll hand over sample snippets.
02:15 Marco Alvarez: Any differences in function-calling? We rely on structured JSON responses mapped to our internal schema.
02:21 Jordan Lee: Function-calling works similarly; Redwood's runtime supports returning structured JSON and can enforce output shape via validators. Small caveat: for heavy structured outputs we sometimes recommend a two-pass approach or using JSON schema hints to improve determinism 
- we can show examples.
02:40 Lisa Chen: On security, can the hosted sandbox integrate with our KMS? We need key custody and encryption-at-rest controls.
02:46 Alex Kim: For private deployments yes. Hosted can support customer-managed keys for encrypted payloads via KMS integrations 
- we'll share the KMS integration guide. Audit logs and RBAC are available in Redwood Console; log retention configurable as an add-on.
03:00 Priya Singh: Benchmarks 
- what will you run?
03:03 Jordan Lee: We'll run a 5k request benchmark that mirrors your token distributions; measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and token cost. We'll compare config variants: hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (baseline), dedicated pool with batching tuned, and a quantized model variant if you want to test cost tradeoffs. Expect initial results within 10 business days of receiving dataset and sample traffic patterns.
03:28 Marco Alvarez: Do you support streaming responses? We have a UI that streams tokens for user-facing features.
03:33 Alex Kim: Yes, streaming is supported via both OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs. Note: streaming latency characteristics differ; we'll include streaming benchmarks.
03:42 Priya Singh: We also need function/tool calling to call our internal retrieval service; how does Redwood handle tool security?
03:49 Jordan Lee: Tool calls can be proxied through your VPC or via secure connector; secrets never stored in plaintext in Redwood. We can set up a canary route to your retrieval microservice during POC.
03:59 Priya Singh: Good. Any limitations on structured output size?
04:02 Jordan Lee: Large structured payloads impact token usage; if you expect huge JSON blobs we recommend compressing or returning references. For most structured extraction tasks you're describing, we've seen good determinism with schema hints and function-calling.
04:16 Lisa Chen: Compliance: can you share SOC2 report and pen test summaries? Also need data residency for EU customers.
04:23 Alex Kim: We'll share SOC2 and ISO docs; video caveat, hosted regions include EU and NA. Private on-prem/VPC option available for strict residency.
04:35 Priya Singh: Timeline 
- we want a 4-week POC. Week1 integration + sandbox keys, week2 run benchmarks, week3 tuning, week4 evaluate + exec decision. Can Redwood commit to that?
04:47 Alex Kim: Yes that's our typical cadence. Jordan will own week2 benchmark runs and tuning. We'll provide SOW and success criteria template today.
04:55 Marco Alvarez: What about cost modeling? We need a clear per-token and per-hour cost to compare to building in-house.
04:59 Jordan Lee: We'll provide a cost model spreadsheet based on your token volumes and concurrency. We'll include options: hosted, dedicated, quantized models. We'll also show how batching and KV cache reduce per-token cost.
05:15 Priya Singh: Any concerns? I guess we'll need red-team review on tool calling. Also want to ensure latency under 700ms p95 
- is that realistic?
05:24 Jordan Lee: For 1-2k token outputs p95 700ms is aggressive but achievable with dedicated GPUs and tuned batching; hosted can hit it for smaller outputs. We'll test.
05:34 Alex Kim: If latency becomes an issue, fallback to a smaller/quantized model variant is an option 
- Redwood supports automated fallback routing.
05:42 Marco Alvarez: For SDKs, please include retry semantics and idempotency guidance 
- we need to know how to handle partial failures.
05:49 Jordan Lee: We'll add sample retry/backoff code and idempotency keys in the SDK examples.
05:55 Priya Singh: Great. Anything else?
05:57 Alex Kim: We'll send links: deck (https://redwood.example/sales/zenith-deck.pdf), benchmark spreadsheet (https://redwood.example/benchmarks/zenith-bench.xlsx), and sample SDK repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/zenith).
06:10 Lisa Chen: I'll review the security docs and come back with questions.
06:13 Alex Kim: Recap: 4-week POC, deliverables from Redwood: SOW, security docs, sandbox keys, SDK snippets, benchmark plan. From Zenith: dataset + schema, infra constraints, security review. Action items captured.
06:25 Priya Singh: Ok thanks, we'll prioritize getting the dataset+schema to you by 2026-07-09.
06:30 Alex Kim: Thanks everyone 
- we'll follow up with SOW and next meeting invite for the technical deep dive.

Links/Artifacts referenced:

End of transcript.
